dimensions.evidence: The Title input sits at the top of a clear two-column layout: the form is on the left and the metadata sidebar (Labels, Milestone, Projects, Assignees) is on the right. The blue 'Create Issue' button is aligned bottom-right of the form. The sidebar sections are split by dividers.
dimensions.justification: The grouping and reading order are clear and the main action is easy to find. There is no page heading such as 'New Issue', though, and the Labels section in the sidebar is visually weak. Its only cue is a small gear icon, so the label step does not stand out.

dimensions.evidence: The Write/Preview tabs, markdown toolbar, sidebar with gear icons and 'Create Issue' button follow GitHub/Gitea conventions. Capitalisation is mixed: 'No Milestone' and 'No Assignees' versus 'No labels' and 'No projects'.
dimensions.justification: The layout matches what users expect from Git platforms. The only problem is the inconsistent capitalisation of the empty-state text.

dimensions.evidence: The repo breadcrumb 'judge-demo / web-shop' is shown, the Issues tab is active with the counter 4, and the Title input has a focus ring. The sidebar shows the current state of each field ('No labels', 'No Milestone').
dimensions.justification: Users can see where they are and what state the metadata is in. The page has no explicit 'New issue' title, so the user has to infer the context from the empty form.

dimensions.evidence: Labels and button text are short and clear: 'Title', 'Leave a comment', 'Drop files here to upload', 'Create Issue'. 'No Branch/Tag Specified' is jargon and its purpose is unclear.
dimensions.justification: Most labels are plain. 'Leave a comment' is an odd placeholder for an issue description, and the branch/tag dropdown has no explanation.

dimensions.evidence: The Title field is identified only by placeholder text that disappears when typing. It has no required marker. 'Create Issue' looks enabled while the title is empty, and there is no hint about required fields.
dimensions.justification: Users only find out the title is required when they try to submit. A placeholder used as the label also stops helping once text is entered.

dimensions.evidence: The title field has focus on load. The markdown toolbar, @-mention and file drop zone are visible, and all metadata pickers are on the same page.
dimensions.justification: The whole task (title, description, label) can be done on one page. Adding a label requires finding the small gear icon instead of an obvious control, which is a small extra cost.

dimensions.evidence: The page is a clean dark theme with few elements. The toolbar has many icons and there is a large empty area below the form.
dimensions.justification: The density suits the task. Nothing unnecessary competes with the form.

dimensions.evidence: Placeholder text ('Title', 'Leave a comment') and the secondary sidebar text ('No labels') are grey on a dark background with low contrast. The gear icons are small (about 16px). White text on the light-blue 'Create Issue' button looks low in contrast. The Title field has no visible label.
dimensions.justification: Several elements look likely to fail WCAG 1.4.3 and 1.4.11 contrast, and the target size of the gear icons is borderline under 2.5.8. Relying on placeholders instead of labels hurts screen-reader users and users with memory difficulties.

strengths: A familiar two-column issue form that matches GitHub conventions, with all metadata on one page
The title field has focus on load and the 'Create Issue' button is clearly placed
Clear location context: repo breadcrumb and active Issues tab with counter

recommendations.recommendation: Add a persistent visible 'Title' label with a required asterisk. Disable 'Create Issue', or show an inline message, while the title is empty.
Increase the contrast of placeholder text, the sidebar empty-state text and the primary button (aim for at least 4.5:1). Enlarge the gear-icon targets to at least 24×24px.
Make the sidebar headers ('Labels', etc.) fully clickable and add an explicit 'Add label' affordance instead of relying on the gear icon alone.
Change the 'Leave a comment' placeholder to 'Describe the issue…', add a tooltip explaining 'No Branch/Tag Specified', and make the empty-state capitalisation consistent.
Add a 'New issue' page heading above the form.

dimensions.evidence: The form uses a clear two-column layout: title, editor, upload area and the blue 'Create Issue' button sit in the main column, with a metadata sidebar (Labels, Milestone, Projects, Assignees) on the right. The Title field is focused at the top.
dimensions.justification: The layout follows a clear F-pattern and the primary action stands out. There is no page heading such as 'New Issue', and in the dark theme the sidebar sections look about as heavy as the main form.

dimensions.evidence: The Write/Preview tabs, markdown toolbar, sidebar with gear icons and 'Create Issue' button match GitHub/Gitea conventions. Repo tabs and icons match the rest of the app.
dimensions.justification: This is the standard Git-platform issue form pattern, and components are used consistently.

dimensions.evidence: The 'Issues 4' tab is underlined and the 'judge-demo / web-shop' breadcrumb is visible, but the page has no 'New Issue' heading. The sidebar shows its current state ('No labels', 'No Milestone').
dimensions.justification: Users know which repo and section they are in, but nothing explicitly says this is a new-issue form. Fix: add a 'New Issue' heading or breadcrumb segment.

dimensions.evidence: The description placeholder says 'Leave a comment', which fits replies better than a new issue description. Capitalisation is inconsistent ('No labels' vs 'No Milestone' / 'No Assignees'). 'No Branch/Tag Specified' assumes Git knowledge. Toolbar icons have no visible labels.
dimensions.justification: Most labels are clear, but the description placeholder is misleading and the capitalisation is inconsistent. Fix: use 'Describe the issue…' and sentence case throughout.

dimensions.evidence: The Title field relies only on the placeholder 'Title' and has no required marker. 'Create Issue' looks active even though the title is empty. There is no format hint or template guidance.
dimensions.justification: Users get no warning that the title is required, and the placeholder disappears once they start typing. Fix: add a persistent 'Title *' label, mark it as required, and disable the button or validate inline.

dimensions.evidence: Labels can only be added through a small gear icon next to 'Labels' in the sidebar. The markdown toolbar, @-mention and drag-and-drop upload are available. The title field is autofocused.
dimensions.justification: Creating an issue takes few steps, but the label task depends on spotting a small gear icon with no text affordance. Fix: make the whole 'Labels' row clickable, or add an 'Add labels' link.

dimensions.evidence: The form is clean with lots of whitespace. The footer shows developer details ('Page: 11ms Template: 4ms'), and the empty area below the form is unused.
dimensions.justification: There is little clutter. The diagnostic footer is the only minor noise.

dimensions.evidence: Placeholders ('Title', 'Leave a comment') are low-contrast grey on the dark background. The gear icons are about 16px, which is a small target. The white text on the light-blue 'Create Issue' button looks borderline. The toolbar is icon-only, and the input borders are faint.
dimensions.justification: Placeholders are used as labels, several targets are small, and some contrast looks below 4.5:1. Fix: add visible labels, increase contrast and enlarge the gear targets.

strengths: Familiar Git-platform issue layout with the metadata sidebar kept separate from the content
Rich markdown editor with Write/Preview tabs and drag-and-drop file upload
Clear primary action and active Issues tab

recommendations.recommendation: Add a persistent visible 'Title' label with a required marker, and validate inline or disable 'Create Issue' until a title is entered.
Make the Labels (and other sidebar) headers fully clickable with an explicit 'Add labels' affordance instead of a small gear icon only.
Raise contrast for placeholders, input borders and the primary button text to meet WCAG 1.4.3/1.4.11, and enlarge the sidebar gear targets to at least 24×24px.
Add a 'New Issue' page heading so the form's purpose is explicit.
Change the description placeholder to 'Describe the issue…' and use consistent capitalisation in the sidebar empty states.

dimensions.evidence: The two-column layout puts the main form on the left (Title, Write/Preview editor, upload zone, blue 'Create Issue' button at the bottom right) and the metadata sidebar on the right (Labels, Milestone, Projects, Assignees, separated by dividers).
dimensions.justification: The grouping is clear and follows the F-pattern, and the primary action stands out. There is no page heading such as 'New Issue', and the Title field looks no more important than the description area, so the hierarchy has small gaps.

dimensions.evidence: The repo header, the tab bar with 'Issues 4' active, and the gear icons on every sidebar section look like the rest of Gitea and match GitHub's new-issue layout (Write/Preview tabs, a markdown toolbar, a metadata sidebar).
dimensions.justification: Components, icons and naming are the same everywhere on the page and follow Git platform conventions.

dimensions.evidence: The 'Issues' tab is underlined and the 'judge-demo / web-shop' breadcrumb is visible. The sidebar shows the current state ('No labels', 'No Milestone', 'No Assignees'). There is no 'New Issue' title or breadcrumb step.
dimensions.justification: The user knows which repo and section they are in, but nothing names this as the issue-creation page. The empty sidebar states are shown clearly.

dimensions.evidence: The labels 'Title', 'Leave a comment', 'Drop files here to upload' and 'Create Issue' are plain. 'No Branch/Tag Specified' is jargon, and its purpose on an issue is unclear. 'Leave a comment' is an odd placeholder for an issue description.
dimensions.justification: Most labels are clear. A few wordings could confuse newcomers.

dimensions.evidence: The Title field is the only input that must be filled in, but it only shows the placeholder 'Title', with no asterisk or 'required' label. The 'Create Issue' button already looks enabled while the title is empty. No format hints are shown.
dimensions.justification: Users can't see what is required until they submit, and once they start typing the placeholder disappears, so the field loses its label. Fix: add a persistent 'Title *' label and disable the button or validate inline.

dimensions.evidence: Labels are changed through a small gear icon at 1328,241. The text 'No labels' does not look clickable. The markdown toolbar and Preview tab are easy to reach.
dimensions.justification: Adding a label, which is part of the typical task, requires finding a small, unlabeled gear icon. That is not obvious and slows the task down. Fix: make the whole section header or 'No labels' clickable, or add an 'Add label' link.

dimensions.evidence: The form is compact and has a clean dark theme. The toolbar has 16 icons, and the right sidebar uses its space well. The lower half of the viewport is empty.
dimensions.justification: There is very little clutter. The toolbar is dense but standard for a markdown editor.

dimensions.evidence: The grey placeholders ('Title', 'Leave a comment') and the grey footer text sit on a dark background with low contrast. The sidebar gear icons are about 16px, which is close to the WCAG 2.5.8 minimum target size of 24px. The title field shows a visible blue focus border. The 'Create Issue' button pairs white text with a mid-blue background, so its contrast is borderline.
dimensions.justification: Several elements look like they fall below contrast and target-size guidance. The focus indicator is a positive. Fix: raise placeholder contrast, add visible labels and make the gear targets larger.

strengths: A familiar GitHub-like layout: the form and metadata sidebar make issue creation easy to recognise.
A full markdown editor with a Write/Preview toggle and a drag-and-drop upload zone.
A clear primary 'Create Issue' button and a visible focus state on the Title field.

recommendations.recommendation: Add a persistent visible label 'Title' with a required marker, and validate it inline or disable 'Create Issue' until a title is entered.
Make the Labels, Milestone, Projects and Assignees headers or their 'No …' text clickable, or add explicit 'Add label' actions, instead of relying on small gear icons.
Raise placeholder and secondary text contrast to at least 4.5:1 and enlarge the gear icon targets to 24×24px or more.
Add a page heading or breadcrumb step 'New Issue' above the form.
Change the placeholder 'Leave a comment' to 'Describe the issue' and add a tooltip explaining the 'No Branch/Tag Specified' selector.
